summary: Unexpected multi-region auth retries after token refresh for residency-pinned tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Lexify Apps, Dedicated) reports intermittent spikes in API p95 latency and increased per-request auth retries following scheduled token rotation for residency-pinned tenant. Traffic should remain in eu-west; instead some requests observed to reauthenticate against US control plane and then failover back to EU, causing auth retries and TLS handshakes that increase p95.

Impact:
- Customer experiences ~10-30% of requests with auth retries and increased p95 (observed +220ms on p95) during rotation windows.
- Affects production inference calls to redwood-v0.9 and llama-2-70b for the tenant.
- Customer is concerned about data egress to US and potential residency violation.

Environment:
- Tenant: lexify-prod (dedicated capacity)
- Region: prod/eu-west primary; burst fallback allowed to us-west-2 but should not occur during strict residency windows.
- SDK/agent: lexify-internal-sdk v1.4.2

Observed behavior:
1) Control plane issues a token rotation for tenant at ~2026-03-10T02:00Z.
2) Some edge proxies continue to route client connections to EU edges, but token verification calls (control-plane auth) briefly hit us-west-2 control plane replicas.
3) SDK observes 401 on first attempt, retries token exchange; second attempt succeeds against EU but only after an additional swap through US causing extra round trip and TLS rehandshake.
4) Result: increased auth retry count, spike in p95 latency and intermittent cross-region egress observed in packet captures.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
- Heavy inference batch during rotation window (they schedule rotations every 24h).
- Tail requests show auth_retry_count >= 1 and traces show control-plane auth endpoint resolved to us-west-2 for ~10% of requests.

Expected:
- Token rotation should be served by EU control-plane replicas for eu-west tenancy and should not cause cross-region auth calls or retries for pinned tenants.

Observed logs and artifacts (attached by customer):
- sample_trace_ids: [trace-eu-1001, trace-eu-1013, trace-eu-1034]
- packet_capture_snippet: base64:AAECAwQFBgc... (redacted)
- client_sdk_logs: "auth: token_exchange: attempt=1 endpoint=auth.eu-west.redwood.internal status=401; attempt=2 endpoint=auth.us-west-2.redwood.internal status=200"
logs: 2026-03-10T02:00:14Z edge-proxy-eu-west: auth-call to auth.us-west-2.redwood.internal (resolved by DNS) for tenant=lexify-prod
2026-03-10T02:00:15Z serving-runtime: request p95 increased from 180ms to 410ms (sample window 60s)
investigation_notes: 03/10 04:00 UTC - SRE: Verified token-rotation event correlates with spike window. Control plane rollout log shows staggered rollout across replicas: eu-west-primary, eu-west-replica-1, us-west-2-replica.

03/10 05:10 UTC - Networking: DNS observation: some EU edges resolved auth.* hostnames to US replica during rotation due to short-lived DNS cache eviction and round-robin result from shared SRV records.

03/10 06:00 UTC - Auth team hypothesis: token swap created a brief window where EU replicas rejected legacy token signatures until their local cache warmed; SDKs retried and DNS influenced which replica served the retry.
03/11 09:30 UTC - Control plane: Found a concurrent control-plane rollout job that updated SRV entries order; PR 4123 introduced a faster propagation but did not pin SRV preference per tenancy.
timeline: 2026-03-10T03:15 - SRE alerted, started correlation with rotation events
2026-03-11T09:00 - Control plane team reproduced race locally using test tenant and confirmed SRV shuffle can cause cross-region retry path
2026-03-12T08:00 - mitigation patch staged to pin SRV order for residency-pinned tenants (canary)
comments: 2026-03-10 07:05 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged with customer, requested packet captures and sample trace IDs. Escalated to SRE and Auth teams.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (Lexify Support): Provided SDK logs and pcap. Notes they see ~12% of requests hit us-west-2 during rotation windows and are concerned about egress. Asked for temporary mitigation.

2026-03-11 10:15 - SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally. Short-lived DNS shuffle combined with token cache cold-start appears to cause retry path to US. Creating control-plane fix to ensure tenancy SRV affinity during token rotation.
2026-03-12 08:25 - Support (Aisha): Deployed canary mitigation for lexify-prod to pin SRV order to eu-west replicas. Requested customer to monitor and report p95 for next rotation window.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Customer (Lexify Support): Confirmed immediate reduction in cross-region auth hits to ~0.6% in canary traffic. Still monitoring for full rotation next day.
workaround: Canary mitigation: pin SRV resolution order for tenancy lexify-prod to EU replicas and increase local token cache warmup window during rotation. Applied to lexify-prod on 2026-03-12 08:25 UTC.
resolution_plan:
Short term: Roll out SRV-pin canary to all dedicated tenants with strict residency and add a 30s token-cache warmup lock during rotation.
Medium term: Control-plane change to publish SRV entries with tenancy-scoped priority and ensure DNS TTL behavior does not cause cross-region fallback during rotations (PR 4123 follow-up).
Long term: Add pre-signed rotation handoff so edges can pre-warm tokens before rotation cutover.
status_update: Canary shows expected reduction in cross-region auth retries for lexify-prod. Control plane follow-up PR being prepared; target full rollout after 48h of canary stability.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation applied 2026-03-12; customer reported immediate improvement. Follow-up control plane PR scheduled and SRE to validate across other tenants. No policy violation observed; temporary pin avoids US egress during rotation for affected tenant.
follow_up_tasks: CP-PR-4123-followup: Ensure SRV priority is tenancy-aware and respects residency pinning
OBS-1128: Add metric auth.retry.location_switch_count per tenant
DOCS-224: Document token rotation behavior and recommended customer rotation windows
